speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the manpower crunch and constraints in the public sector, what more can be done by the Home Team to leverage on new technology to detect and deter crime, and to assist with typically manpower-intensive investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Leveraging on technology is one of the ways, as articulated at the start of the session.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These have reduced crime in our HDB estates and helped Police solve cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also leverage on crowdsourcing technology, so members of the public can play a part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I mentioned earlier about the app – Police@SG app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will enable close to real-time submission of information that can help facilitate investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I also spoke earlier about another initiative known as the Vehicle on Watch Scheme, which was launched last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This adds extra eyes in our HDB carparks to deter crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police may approach participating car owners for footage, if needed to solve cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police have also redesigned the Neighbourhood Police Posts (NPPs) and used technology to facilitate round-the-clock automated services for residents, while allowing police officers to be re-deployed from desk-bound duties to other frontline tasks, such as patrols and walking on the beat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: With better information gathering, we will invest in stronger sense-making capabilities, such as video and data analytics, so that richer and more timely information is provided to our officers while responding to incidents, or when conducting investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Data from different sources will be aggregated and analysed real-time to detect potential threats and criminal activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Advanced data analytics can help us to analyse data, discern patterns, and deploy our resources dynamically and in the most optimal way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will be better able to adopt a tiered and differentiated front-line response model, channelling resources to where they are most needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will enable us to enhance the safety and security of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, would the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) consider focusing the angle of the CCTV also onto staircase entry points?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for the size of bins, this is something we certainly will look at, in terms of the overall analysis of threats.
